title: Best Resources for HD2D Pixel Art Models and Animations?
author: Kooker321
selftext:
I'm working on an HD2D party rpg game in the style of Octopath Traveler and Final Fantasy Resonance. I'm using Claude Code Opus and Godot. 

The AI generated art is fairly underwhelming at this stage, though it might improve after some more iterations. That being said, I'm exploring options to adopt more tools like PixelLab or assets from the marketplace (though these seem to be pretty limited on itch.io unfortunately). 

Which tools and resources have you been using to take your pixel art and animations to the next level?

comments.author: StarMonkeyGames
comments.body:
I haven't seen one singular place that can do it all. I use a combination of Pixel Lab and OpenAI/Claude/Whatever

Pixel Labs allows you to API, so I hooked it up to my GPT chat session and iterate much faster.

Then I go and have AI remake problematic frames with python tools first. Like editting. Not regenerating.

Or I do it myself or both. 

If that doesn't work. Then regenerate drawings using the best model with another agent double checker.

Then I use the API to organize it back into Pixel. 

And it gets the animations there. A descent UI / export options.   
  
 It mostly works, like it's on the edge of doable and with time, it will get easier and easier.

replies.author: Kooker321
replies.body:
Thanks, that's helpful! Is your main work flow text generation of assets with Claude Code connected to Pixel Lab with API? Maybe with some reference images thrown in, plus a lot of iteration? How does Claude on its own compare to Claude with Pixel Lab?

I see there are other tools out there that people promote to help with things like animation, but I can't tell if they're legit or just self promotion.

replies.author: StarMonkeyGames
replies.body:
Yeah it's more or less what you said. I used references and skeleton features. It kind of works. Sometimes there are limitations.

But really it's mostly iteration. This method lets you go generate much faster, then you can organize those results easier. Like you download the entire sprite sheet. Feed it back into your chat session

Then be like mix and match. Then replace from the chat session back into their UI.

You got a trailer for your game yet?
